confirmed.title: REGRESSION (slice-cv-04, broken by the slice-cvcr3-01 fix): the footer highlight 'motorsport / F1, music, esports →' turns muted #5f5b54 on hover and keyboard focus
confirmed.expected: The footer highlight text stays #1c1b19 (rgb(28, 27, 25)) at rest, on hover and on focus. Only the background changes, to rgba(255,196,40,.95). In the prototype the footer span has inline color:#1c1b19, and its style-hover changes only the background.
confirmed.actual: At rest it is rgb(28, 27, 25), which is correct. On hover and on :focus-visible it computes to rgb(95, 91, 84). The round-3 fix added `color: inherit` to `.yellow:hover, .yellow:focus-visible` (Highlight.module.css:18-22), with specificity (0,2,0). That beats `.footer a { color: var(--ink) }` (CvSheet.module.css:134-136, specificity (0,1,1)), so the link inherits the footer paragraph's muted colour (CvSheet.module.css:128-129). The other three yellow highlights are unaffected because their parent (.entryTitle) inherits ink.
confirmed.evidence: Playwright on the served out/ build at 1280x1000, /#cv: hovering `#sheet-cv a:has-text('motorsport')` gives color 'rgb(95, 91, 84)' and background 'rgba(255, 196, 40, 0.95)'. Hovering 'Founder & Lead Engineer' gives 'rgb(28, 27, 25)'. Keyboard focus (Tab to the footer link) also gives color rgb(95, 91, 84). No e2e test hovers a highlight and reads its colour, so the gates did not catch this (the only hover test in e2e/pile.spec.ts is the tab one at line 108).
confirmed.suggestedFix: Stop the hover rule from forcing inherit over the footer override. Either change CvSheet.module.css `.footer a` to a selector that outranks it, such as `.footer a, .footer a:hover, .footer a:focus-visible { color: var(--ink); }`, or drop `color: inherit` from `.yellow:hover` and instead neutralise the global rule for highlights with `.highlight:hover { color: inherit }` placed before the footer override. Add a Playwright test that hovers and focuses each of the 4 yellow highlights plus the purple one and asserts color rgb(28, 27, 25).
confirmed.verifyReasoning: Reproduced on the served out/ build at 1280x1000, /#cv. The footer 'motorsport' link (class Highlight_highlight Highlight_yellow) is rgb(28,27,25) at rest. On hover it is rgb(95,91,84) with background rgba(255,196,40,0.95). On keyboard focus (:focus-visible true) it is also rgb(95,91,84). Cause: Highlight.module.css:18-22 `.yellow:hover, .yellow:focus-visible { color: inherit }` has specificity (0,2,0), which beats CvSheet.module.css:134-136 `.footer a { color: var(--ink) }` at (0,1,1). The link therefore inherits `.footer { color: var(--muted) }` (CvSheet.module.css:128-129). Prototype line 175 gives the footer span inline color:#1c1b19, and its style-hover changes only the background.
confirmed.fix: In src/components/sheets/CvSheet.module.css:134, change the selector to `.footer a, .footer a:hover, .footer a:focus-visible { color: var(--ink); }` (specificity (0,2,1) outranks .yellow:hover). Add an e2e test that hovers and focuses the footer highlight and asserts color rgb(28, 27, 25).

confirmed.title: Racing GPS polaroid shows a different crop from the reference: the view is shifted about 10% of the image width to the right and 2% up, so the browser bar and the dark side panel show and the track is not centred
confirmed.expected: The crop from the reference image-slot (s:1.8, x:+18, y:+50, applied the way reference/image-slot.js _applyView does it at lines 1034-1040: the image is sized to cover x scale, and its centre sits at left 50+x %, top 50+y % of the frame). For the 161x348 asset in a 300x300 frame, the visible window covers image x 12.2%-67.8% and image y 24.3%-50.0% (centre 40% / 37.15%). This is the track-centred crop the prototype renders, with no browser toolbar at the top.
confirmed.actual: imageCrop { scale: 1.8, objectPosition: '58% 22%' } (content.ts:246), applied in RacingSheet.tsx:37 as object-fit:cover plus transform:scale(1.8) around the frame centre. The visible window is image x 22.2%-77.8% and y 22.1%-47.8% (centre 50% / 35%). The object-position x value has no effect, because under cover the image width equals the frame width. The render shows the laptop's browser tab/address bar across the top, the dark right-hand panel with its orange text, and the blue track in the left third instead of the centre.
confirmed.evidence: I served the reference prototype through a Playwright route on the same origin, dismissed the intro, clicked the racing tab, and took screenshots of the prototype and of the build at 1280px (identical stage position: 238,99, 760 wide). Side-by-side crop: scratchpad/review-r4/slice-racing-video-about-tabs/gps-proto-vs-impl.png (from proto-racing-1280.png and impl-racing-1280.png). Every other Racing, Video and About text box matched the prototype to under 0.6px. The only geometry difference was this image: proto #img1 [403.9,653,300,300] vs impl [283.9,533,540.1,540.1]. That is the expected scale box, but the image content is offset. implementation-notes' deviation log says the literal pan 'produced a wrong crop'. That premise does not hold: the prototype's image-slot math turns the literal values into the centred crop above, and that crop can be reproduced exactly.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Keep scale 1.8 and move the window to match the reference. In RacingSheet.tsx:37 use style={{ objectPosition: '50% 26.1%', transform: 'scale(1.8) translateX(10%)' }}. Store these in content.ts:246, e.g. imageCrop: { scale: 1.8, objectPosition: '50% 26.1%', translate: '10%, 0' }. Or port the image-slot formula directly: img position:absolute; width:180%; height:389%; left:68%; top:100%; transform:translate(-50%,-50%); no object-fit. Then update the deviation-log entry.
confirmed.verifyReasoning: I reproduced this on the current build (port 5203). The img has naturalWidth 161 and naturalHeight 348, and computed styles object-fit:cover, object-position '58% 22%', transform matrix(1.8,0,0,1.8,0,0) inside a 300x300 frame (content.ts:246, RacingSheet.tsx:37). Under cover the rendered width equals the frame width, so the 58% x value does nothing and the visible window is centred at image x 50%. I checked the reference math in image-slot.js:1034-1040: width = base*s*iw/fw = 180%, height = 389%, left = 50+18 = 68%, top = 50+50 = 100%, plus translate(-50%,-50%) (image-slot.js:299). That makes the visible window image x 12.2%-67.8% and y 24.3%-50.0%, centred at (40%, 37.15%). I rendered both crops side by side with the real asset (scratchpad/review-r4/verify-gps/ref-vs-impl.png). The reference crop puts the blue GPS trace near the centre, with a little of the left dark panel showing. The build crop pushes the trace into the left third and shows the right-hand dark panel with its orange text. README.md:167 says the image should be 'centred on the track' and README.md:261 says 'shifted so the track is centred'. The deviation note in implementation-notes.md:19 is the implementer's own workaround, not an owner decision. Its premise, that the literal pan cannot be reproduced through cover, is false, because the formula maps exactly as shown. The effect is purely visual on a low-res placeholder asset, so low severity is correct.
confirmed.fix: In src/content.ts:246 change imageCrop to { scale: 1.8, objectPosition: '50% 26.1%', translateX: '10%' } and add translateX to its type. In src/components/sheets/RacingSheet.tsx:37 apply style={{ objectPosition, transform: `scale(${scale}) translateX(${translateX})` }}. The translate runs in pre-scale units, 10% of the frame width, which equals 10% of the image width under cover, so the view centre moves from image x 50% to 40%. Object-position y 26.1% moves the centre to (50+116*0.261)/216 = 37.15%. The result matches the reference window of x 12.2-67.8% and y 24.3-50.0%. Also update the comment at content.ts:238-245 and the deviation entry at docs/implementation-notes.md:19 so they describe the exact mapping of the reference pan (s 1.8, x +18, y +50).

confirmed.title: NOT-FIXED (behaviour-03): the reduced-motion sheet swap is still a hard cut, not a cross-fade. The incoming sheet's opacity never meaningfully drops below 1
confirmed.expected: README Accessibility and bh-13: under prefers-reduced-motion, a sheet swap is an instant cross-fade. The incoming sheet should visibly fade from about 0 to 1 over Sheet.module.css's `transition: opacity 0.2s`, and some frame should show 0 < opacity < 1 (this was the round-3 fix's own acceptance criterion).
confirmed.actual: The round-3 fix (da95c86) starts the move at stage 'out' with inline opacity 0 and switches to 'in' (opacity 1) 16ms later. But a hidden sheet's resting style (sheetStyle's last branch, pile.ts:102) has opacity 1. Going hidden to 'out' therefore starts a 1 -> 0 transition that is only about 16ms in when 'in' reverses it back to 1. Measured live at 1440x900 with reducedMotion:'reduce', sampling getComputedStyle(sheet).opacity every rAF: racing = 1.0000 at every frame (z 0 -> 9 -> 11 -> 10), video = 1.0000 at every frame, about = a single frame at 0.7787, then 0.9914, then 1. The same happens after a live switch to reduced motion (emulateMedia mid-session): racing stays at 1.000 in every frame. The incoming sheet goes from under the top sheet (z 9) to over it (z 11) at full opacity, so it is still a cut. Unit tests pass because they check only the inline style values, and no e2e test samples the computed opacity.
confirmed.evidence: Playwright script (scratchpad review-r4/behaviour-a11y-responsive/t6.cjs) with a MutationObserver plus per-frame sampling of sheet-racing: style attr at +104ms 'z-index: 9; ... opacity: 0;', at +127ms 'z-index: 11; ... opacity: 1;'. The computed opacity rows are 120ms '0 1.0000 9 visible' and 134ms '1 1.0000 11 visible'. min visible opacity is 1 for racing and video, and 0.7787 for about. Code: usePile.ts:35 REDUCED_OUT_MS = 16, usePile.ts:160-165 (the out -> in switch after 16ms), pile.ts:102 `return { transform: STRAIGHT_TRANSFORM, z: 0, visible: false, opacity: 1 }`.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Make the incoming sheet's pre-fade state actually 0. In pile.ts sheetStyle, return `opacity: reducedMotion ? 0 : 1` for the hidden branch (line 102). The 'out' stage then already starts at 0 with no reverse transition, and the switch to 'in' runs the full 0 -> 1 fade over 0.2s. Or keep the 'out' stage (opacity 0) for at least the 0.2s transition before switching to 'in'. Add an e2e test under reducedMotion:'reduce' that samples getComputedStyle(incoming).opacity per rAF after a tab click and asserts that some frame is between 0.05 and 0.95.
confirmed.verifyReasoning: Reproduced on the current out/ build at 1440x900 with reducedMotion:'reduce' on port 5204. I sampled getComputedStyle(#sheet-racing) on every animation frame after clicking the racing tab. The opacity was 1.000 in every frame while z-index went 0 (hidden) -> 9 (visible) -> 11 -> 10, so the minimum visible opacity was 1. For about, the minimum was 0.779 in one frame, then 0.992, then 1.000. The code explains it. Hidden sheets keep opacity 1 (pile.ts:101, `return { transform: STRAIGHT_TRANSFORM, z: 0, visible: false, opacity: 1 }`) and are hidden only by `.hidden { visibility: hidden }` (Sheet.module.css:29-30), not display:none. So the 'out' stage (pile.ts:92, opacity 0) starts a 1 -> 0 transition under `transition: opacity 0.2s` (Sheet.module.css:35). usePile.ts:35 REDUCED_OUT_MS = 16 then switches to 'in' (opacity 1) about one frame later and reverses that transition while opacity is still about 1. Also, during 'out' the incoming sheet sits at z m+1, under the top sheet at m+2, so it is not seen anyway. When it jumps to z m+3 it appears at full opacity. That is still a hard cut and violates README:238 and bh-13 ('instant cross-fade'). Severity low is right because it only affects reduced-motion users and is cosmetic.
confirmed.fix: In src/lib/pile.ts sheetStyle, change the hidden branch (line 101) to `return { transform: STRAIGHT_TRANSFORM, z: 0, visible: false, opacity: reducedMotion ? 0 : 1 };` so a hidden sheet already rests at opacity 0 under reduced motion. The 'out' -> 'in' switch then runs a real 0 -> 1 fade over 0.2s. The 'in' sheet is at z m+3, above the outgoing sheet, so this is a true cross-fade. Make sure the outgoing sheet, which becomes hidden at settle, is not visibly faded, since it is already covered. Update the pile.ts unit tests for the hidden-branch opacity. Add an e2e test under emulateMedia({reducedMotion:'reduce'}) that samples getComputedStyle(#sheet-<k>).opacity on each rAF after a tab click and asserts that at least one frame with visibility 'visible' has 0.05 < opacity < 0.95.

confirmed.title: NOT-FIXED (behaviour-03): the reduced-motion sheet swap is still a hard cut; the incoming sheet never shows an opacity below 1
confirmed.expected: Under prefers-reduced-motion, bring() cross-fades the incoming sheet: it starts at opacity 0 and fades to 1 over Sheet.module.css's `transition: opacity .2s`, so some frame shows 0 < opacity < 1 (this is the round-3 behaviour-03 fix, commit da95c86).
confirmed.actual: A hidden sheet gets opacity 1 from sheetStyle's fallback branch (pile.ts:101). The 'out' stage then sets inline opacity 0 (pile.ts:93), which only starts a 1 -> 0 transition. REDUCED_OUT_MS = 16 ms later (usePile.ts:37 and 168), the 'in' stage sets opacity back to 1 and z to m+3. That cancels the barely-started transition, so the sheet lands on top at full opacity in one frame. On the built site (reduced motion, /#cv, click the 'crumbify' tab) every rAF sample of getComputedStyle(#sheet-crumbify).opacity reads '1', including the frames in the 'out' stage. The unit test at src/lib/usePile.test.tsx:269 only checks the state stages ('out' then 'in' after 16 ms), so it passes on this broken behaviour.
confirmed.evidence: Playwright on the served out/ with reducedMotion:'reduce'. A MutationObserver plus rAF sampling on #sheet-crumbify gave: t=852 style 'z-index: 9; ... opacity: 0;' with computed opacity '1'; t=868 and t=871 computed '1', getAnimations().length 1; t=876 style 'z-index: 11; ... opacity: 1;' with computed '1'; every later frame computed '1' with 0 animations. No sample was ever < 1. Script: scratchpad/review-r4/code-quality-security-tests/rm.cjs.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Under reduced motion, a hidden sheet should already have opacity 0: in sheetStyle's last branch return opacity reducedMotion ? 0 : 1. The 'out' stage (opacity 0, z m+1) then causes no transition, and the switch to 'in' (opacity 1) runs the full 0 -> 1 fade over 0.2s. Better still, switch to 'in' after a double requestAnimationFrame rather than a 16 ms timer, so the 'out' style is committed before the change. Add an e2e test under reducedMotion:'reduce' that samples the incoming sheet's computed opacity over rAF after a tab click and asserts that some sample is strictly between 0 and 1.
confirmed.verifyReasoning: Reproduced on the served out/ build (port 5205, reducedMotion 'reduce', /#cv, clicked the visible 'crumbify' tab). I sampled #sheet-crumbify's computed style every rAF: while hidden it reads opacity 1 / visibility hidden / z 0. In the 'out' stage it is visible at z 9 with opacity '1', and from about 300 ms it is visible at z 11 with opacity '1'. Zero visible samples were below 1. The cause is pile.ts:101: the hidden branch returns opacity 1. The reduced 'out' stage (pile.ts:92-93, opacity 0) therefore only starts a 1->0 transition. REDUCED_OUT_MS=16 (usePile.ts:37, 168) then flips the sheet to 'in' (opacity 1, z m+3), which reverses that barely-started transition, so the sheet lands on top at full opacity. README:238 ('make sheet swaps an instant cross-fade') and the round-3 behaviour-03 fix are therefore still not met. The round-3 fix also asked for an e2e check that some frame shows 0 < opacity < 1, and no such test exists. Script: scratchpad/review-r4/verify-code/rm.cjs.
confirmed.fix: In src/lib/pile.ts sheetStyle, make the final hidden branch (line 101) return `opacity: reducedMotion ? 0 : 1`, so a hidden sheet already sits at opacity 0 and the 'out' stage causes no transition. In src/lib/usePile.ts useBring, switch 'out' to 'in' only after the 'out' style has been committed: use a double requestAnimationFrame instead of at(REDUCED_OUT_MS), or keep the 16 ms timer if pile.ts is fixed, since the hidden->out change no longer changes opacity. The 'in' stage (opacity 1) then runs the full 0->1 fade from Sheet.module.css's `transition: opacity 0.2s`. Add a Playwright test with reducedMotion:'reduce': click the crumbify tab, sample getComputedStyle(#sheet-crumbify).opacity each rAF for 400 ms, and assert that some sample has visibility 'visible' and 0 < opacity < 1.

confirmed.title: Two round-3 CSS fixes have no regression test: reverting either one still passes every unit and e2e test
confirmed.expected: Round-3 fixes slice-cvcr3-01 (yellow highlight keeps ink #1c1b19 on hover, via `color: inherit` in `.yellow:hover` at Highlight.module.css:18-22) and slice-new-01 (no outline on the programmatically focused sheet, via `.sheet:focus, .sheet:focus-visible { outline: none }` at Sheet.module.css) each have a test that fails if the fix is removed. The round-3 fix text asked for a Playwright hover test on 'Founder & Lead Engineer'.
confirmed.actual: Highlight.test.tsx:59-66 checks with a regex only that the `.purple:hover` block has color:inherit. No test covers `.yellow:hover`. No unit or e2e test checks the sheet container's outline: the only outline assertion (e2e/pile.spec.ts:357-366) is for the CV contact link. Removing `color: inherit;` from `.yellow:hover` (which brings back the #8a5a00 hover text) or deleting the `.sheet:focus` rule leaves all 114 unit tests and every e2e test green. The fixes themselves work on the current build: hover colour is rgb(28, 27, 25), and #sheet-crumbify has outline-style 'none' after keyboard activation.
confirmed.evidence: grep -rn "outline|yellow" over src/**/*.test.* and e2e matches only Highlight.test.tsx:14/26/37 (render props) and pile.spec.ts:357 (contact link). vitest run gives 18 files and 114 tests passing, and none of them touch these rules. Live check: hover color ['rgb(28, 27, 25)', 'rgba(255, 196, 40, 0.95)'], and after Enter on the highlight, activeElement is sheet-crumbify with outlineStyle 'none'.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Add a regex test in Highlight.test.tsx for the `.yellow:hover, .yellow:focus-visible` block containing color:inherit, like the purple one. Better, add an e2e test that hovers 'Founder & Lead Engineer' and expects color rgb(28, 27, 25). Add an e2e test that focuses a highlight, presses Enter, waits for the move to settle, and expects the computed outlineStyle of document.activeElement (#sheet-crumbify) to be 'none'.
confirmed.verifyReasoning: Highlight.test.tsx:59-66 only regex-checks the `.purple:hover, .purple:focus-visible` block. No test mentions `.yellow:hover`: grep for yellow in tests hits only the render props at lines 14/26/37. The only outline assertion in e2e is pile.spec.ts:357-365, and it covers the CV contact link, not the sheet. SheetFrame.test.tsx:41 checks only tabIndex=-1. So removing `color: inherit` at Highlight.module.css:21, or the `outline: none` rule at Sheet.module.css:26, would not fail any test. This is a real regression-guard gap for two confirmed round-3 fixes, although both fixes currently work.
confirmed.fix: In src/components/Highlight.test.tsx, add a test next to the purple one: match `/\.yellow:hover,\s*\n?\s*\.yellow:focus-visible\s*{([^}]*)}/` and expect the captured block to match /color:\s*inherit/. In e2e/pile.spec.ts, add: (1) hover the 'Founder & Lead Engineer' highlight and expect getComputedStyle color 'rgb(28, 27, 25)'; (2) focus that highlight, press Enter, wait for #sheet-crumbify to be document.activeElement after the move settles, and expect getComputedStyle(activeElement).outlineStyle to be 'none'.
